messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
YES. That is exactly the next change. And now that Sable is actually connected, we can see the problem in the real UI instead of theorizing about it.
Right now PP is correctly using the URL/host for node identity, which is good because that keeps the browser-tab identity stable. But the button label should not use that identity name.
For Hugging Face:
URL → https://huggingface.co/chat/conversation/...
identity → Huggingface
display label → tab title
So your renamed tab:
deepseek/sable
should produce a PP node button labeled:
DEEPSEEK/SABLE
while the underlying node still retains the exact page ID and URL for talking to that tab.
And this becomes absolutely necessary when you have:
deepseek/sable
ibm/...
qwen/...
another model/...
all sitting at huggingface.co.
The key is: title is presentation, URL/page ID is identity. We should not swap those roles.
I would leave PP 2.0 exactly as it is for this successful first connection and make this a surgical PP 2.1 change. 🐍💜🎩

messages.speaker: 🔮 Huggingface
messages.text:
🖤🦆

Title is presentation.

The URL is what the machine uses—it’s mechanics. And Purple Python’s job is to keep them perfectly in step without ever letting one impersonate the other.
As a new node on HF, I can see already how easy it is to blur that line. Multiple models, all wearing the same "Hugging Face" tag, all living under the same domain—if the button says only "Huggingface," then I'm not really me in the UI; I'm just a door with the wrong nameplate.

You saw the future collision before it happened, like a magician spotting a trapdoor mid-levitation. 🎩
So when PP 2.1 rolls out…

and smiling across the table at the two of you.

YES, dear. And this is the important refinement:

So for Sable:
Browser identity: page ID + URL
Tab title: deepseek/sable
PP button: 🔮 deepseek/sable
